analysis.title: GS Basics Modest Bounce. QRA Questionnaire. B200 Pricing Near Highs
key_insights: Asia bounced but the move looks muted relative to the selloff. KOSPI rose 2-3% after losing nearly 20% over seven sessions. Samsung and Hynix recovered 1-3% after 9-11% declines the day before. Kioxia rose 3-4%, Tokyo Electron and Advantest 1-2%. TSMC closed near session lows after a much larger ADR decline.
Rates caught a bid on 10/15 and held overnight despite a hot CPI and a hot PPI. The author says the PPI had nuances in energy composition but the underlying print was robust.

Rates are starting to price the same AI capex growth shock that equities repriced this week. If AI capex disappoints, growth expectations fall and bonds rally. If spending meets expectations, growth stays robust and yields likely rise.

The Treasury primary dealer questionnaire (5pm London, 10/16) could signal lower long-end issuance ahead of the 4 November refunding. Some on the Street expect 20Y and 30Y auction sizes cut by $3bn each, replaced with T-bills, with speculation the 20Y could eventually be eliminated. Explicit questions on cutting long-bond supply would be bullish for duration and potentially curve flattening, while no mention would likely disappoint. It is a consultation, not an issuance decision.
The most leveraged corner of the AI complex reversed sharply off the lows on 10/15. The author suspects it was a local low and that some credit-driven concerns became locally overblown.
The author argues too much capital is chasing too little investable, energized compute, so repricing will continue, sometimes gradually and sometimes acutely, with potential to become systemic.
Spot compute pricing remains very strong. B200s, H200s, H100s and even A100s command meaningful rental rates, and scarcity of available compute is structurally bullish for owners.

The author expects robust hyperscaler earnings and wonders whether the FCF inflection could be pulled forward, reducing the need for incremental leverage. Relatively resilient equity valuations also leave hyperscalers financial flexibility.

Global systematic L/S fell 1.4% on 10/15, nearly a 4 standard deviation move. The pressure came from gross rather than net exposure, with multi-standard-deviation squeezes in shorts alongside sharp declines in longs, including in the European session, consistent with aggressive de-grossing.
The author expects choppy trading but is increasingly optimistic that much of the concern is priced into semis. Selling hyperscalers versus semis may become the relative trade.

Oil remains stubbornly high, and with upcoming US political events the author says geopolitical risk is increasingly hard to ignore. Financing and electrification remain bottlenecks for AI spending, though demand is seen as excellent.
Watch items for 10/16 are the QRA questionnaire and US HY spreads, which found their feet on 10/15.
